summary: Helmer Smith worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Uppsala University and under Karl Ferdinand Johansson, Richard Pischel, and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He served as Dozent at Lund University (1921) and professor at Uppsala University (1936–1947).

Helmut Eimer was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin, the University of Hamburg, and the University of Bonn (where he completed his Promotion under Frank-Richard Hamm), later holding a post at Bonn (~1974–2001).

Helmut Hoffmann specialized in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Freiburg, Humboldt University (Dr. phil. under Heinrich Lüders), and Marburg, he also studied under Giuseppe Tucci and others. His posts included the Prussian Academy, Munich (1948–1968), and Indiana University (1969–1980).

Helmut Krasser worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed his Promotion and Habilitation at the University of Vienna, where he held an appointment (~1989–2014). He also served at the Austrian Academy of Sciences, directing its Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Helmut Rix was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Würzburg, Heidelberg (PhD 1950), and Tübingen (Habilitation). He held posts at Augustana-Hochschule Neuendettelsau (1955), the University of Regensburg (1966), and served as professor at the University of Freiburg (1982–1993).

Helmut Tauscher is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ernst Steinkellner. He has long been affiliated with the University of Vienna (attested 1983, 2010–2015 as professor, and 2026), and served as a Numata visiting professor at Leiden University.

Helmuth von Glasenapp specialized in Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tübingen, Munich, Berlin, and Bonn (PhD under Hermann Jacobi). He was a Privatdozent at Berlin and Bonn, then held chairs at Königsberg (1928–1944) and Tübingen (1946–1959).

Helwig Schmidt-Glintzer is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Göttingen (~1967–1968) and the University of Munich (~1968–1973), later holding positions at the University of Munich (~1979–1993) and the University of Göttingen (~1993–2015).

Hemchandra Raychaudhuri was an Indologist and historian. He served at the University of Calcutta as Carmichael Professor and Head of the Department of Ancient Indian History and Culture (attested 1939) and later of History and Ancient Indian History and Culture (attested 1965).
Hemmige Shriniwasrangachar Biligiri was an Indologist and linguist who served as a professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1991 and 2026).

Henepola Gunaratana is a Buddhist studies scholar and philosopher. He studied at Vidyasekhara Pirivena, Kelaniya, Buddhist Missionary College, and American University (PhD ~1975–1980). He held posts at the Buddhist Institute of Kuala Lumpur, Buddhist Vihara Society, and Georgetown University.

Heng Sure is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Oakland University, UC Berkeley, and the Graduate Theological Union (PhD under Ronald Y. Nakasone), alongside Hsuan Hua. He has held professorial posts at Dharma Realm Buddhist University, GTU, and Bond University.

Henk Blezer is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed his degrees at Leiden University (1987–1997), where he later served as a postdoctoral researcher and university lecturer, alongside a post at the International Institute for Asian Studies (1997–2001).

Henk Bodewitz was an Indologist. He earned his degrees, including a PhD under Jan Gonda, at Utrecht University. He served as assistant professor and chair of Sanskrit at Utrecht University (1966; 1976–1992) and as professor at Leiden University (~1972–1976; 1992–2002).

Henri Bergson was a French philosopher. He studied at Lycée Condorcet, École Normale Supérieure, and the University of Paris. Over his career, he held positions at the lycée David d'Angers (~1881–1883) and the Collège de France (1900–1904).

Henri Cordier was a Sinologist and historian who studied at Lycée Chaptal. He held professorships at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1881–1925) and at Sciences Po (~1886–1925).

Henri Gaidoz was a linguist who studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and under Albrecht Weber in 1865. He taught geography and ethnography at École Libre des Sciences Politiques (1872–1908) and was Directeur d’études in Celtic philology at École Pratique des Hautes Études (1876).

Henri Hubert specialized in religious studies and archaeology. He studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and the École Normale Supérieure. He held posts at the National Archaeological Museum (~1898–1927), the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1900–1927), and the École du Louvre (~1906–1927).

Henri Maspero specialized in Sinology, religious studies, and linguistics, studying at INALCO and under Édouard Chavannes. He worked at EFEO and held chairs in Sinology at the Collège de France (1918–1945), EPHE (~1930–1945), and the Sorbonne/University of Paris (~1944–1945).
Henri Massé was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He held academic posts at the University of Algiers (~1916–1927) and at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (~1927–1958).
